PRIVATISATION_ADV1.label: Advantage: privatisation exposes firms to competitive/profit incentives, raising efficiency

PRIVATISATION_DIS1.label: Disadvantage: may simply replace a public monopoly with an unregulated private monopoly

stages.name: Privatisation
stages.title: Privatisation
stages.sub: Understand privatisation as a development strategy and weigh its benefits against its risks.

steps.q: A country's electricity firm is owned and run by the government, with no clear owner able to sell shares or claim profits. Who bears the risk if it runs at a loss?
steps.wrong: A private owner, using their own money
steps.hint: Nobody holds individual title to the firm, so who ultimately covers its losses?

steps.q: The government now sells this electricity firm to private investors, who take over ownership and control. What has changed hands?
steps.right: Ownership, from the state to private owners
steps.hint: Think about who now legally owns the firm's assets and profits.

steps.q: The new private owners now keep any profit the electricity firm makes, but also lose money if customers switch to a rival supplier. How might this affect how hard they work to cut costs and please customers?
steps.right: They try harder, since profit and survival depend on it
steps.wrong: They try less hard, since government no longer checks on them
steps.hint: Under state ownership there was no personal profit at stake. Now there is.

steps.q: Suppose no rival firm is allowed to build competing power lines, so this newly private electricity firm is still the only supplier in the country. Can customers force it to keep prices fair?
steps.right: No, it can still charge high prices unchecked
steps.wrong: Yes, competition will keep prices fair
